candidatesAccepted.summary: A car gives the most freedom on a shoestring for two people, and the long drive is the main cost. I have not checked road conditions or park gate fees, and access needs were not answered, so this does not account for them.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bus Québec City to Sainte-Anne-des-Monts
candidatesAccepted.summary: A coach avoids driving the long road and keeps the budget low, but I have not verified current timetables or whether service runs on your dates, so check before relying on it. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot say whether this suits them.

candidatesAccepted.title: Shuttle from gateway to park trailhead road
candidatesAccepted.summary: A taxi or pre-arranged shuttle from the gateway town to the park's Mont-Albert side saves the walk on the road and keeps the party's energy for the hut route. I have not checked availability, and whether it can handle your gear is unknown.

candidatesAccepted.title: Chic-Chocs backcountry refuge, Mont-Albert sector
candidatesAccepted.summary: A rustic hut-based base in the Chic-Chocs that fits the rustic night the party accepts and keeps daily walking within their 16 km limit. Not answered: access needs, so accessibility is unknown to me, and I have not checked whether this refuge is open or bookable between 2027-08-15 and 2027-09-15. I cannot account for how it fits their navigation concern in cloud, so they should confirm route marking and whether a guided option exists before relying on it.

candidatesAccepted.title: North-sector Chic-Chocs hut, hut-to-hut option
candidatesAccepted.summary: An alternative hut on the same traverse network, suited to a demanding, rustic three-night plan. Not answered: access needs, and I have not verified seasonal opening or booking requirements for the requested window, so treat it as unconfirmed. Navigation in cloud is not something I can assess for this hut, so check trail conditions and waymarking with the park before committing.

candidatesAccepted.title: Mont Jacques-Cartier summit day
candidatesAccepted.summary: The park's highest peak, a demanding out-and-back over open tundra that suits your appetite for effort. Cloud can close the summit quickly and you asked not to learn navigation in cloud, so go only on a clear forecast or with a guide. Access needs were not answered, and I did not check trail conditions or hut bookings.

candidatesAccepted.title: Guided alpine navigation session
candidatesAccepted.summary: A guided half-day on the plateau to build navigation skills in low visibility before the hut trip, which fits your wish not to learn on the trek. I do not know whether guides run here this season, what they charge, or how far ahead they need booking. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hut-to-hut day section
candidatesAccepted.summary: A single day between two huts on the park's marked trails, within your 16 km daily limit and rustic enough for the one-night-per-hut pattern you described. I have not confirmed hut locations, distances or whether they are open. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hut-to-hut in the Chic-Chocs with a navigation-first plan
candidatesAccepted.summary: Builds on the pair's earlier fair-weather hut trip and fits their demanding effort appetite, but the cloud-navigation concern needs settling before any go decision. Not checked: access needs (not answered), current hut and trail conditions, whether any river crossing stays under the knee-depth limit, and the season window. Trail, hut and reservation status should come from Sépaq, which operates the park, and from park staff. This is an option, not clearance to go.

candidatesAccepted.title: Guided hut traverse in the Chic-Chocs
candidatesAccepted.summary: A licensed guide carries the navigation so the pair does not learn to navigate in cloud on this trip, which is what they said they wanted. The cost band sits well above a shoestring feel, so it is worth weighing against the self-led option. The same unknowns apply: access needs, river crossings, current conditions and season are unchecked, and Sépaq and park staff are the authoritative sources for conditions.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hut booking for the Chic-Chocs route
candidatesAccepted.summary: Securing the three hut nights is the first paperwork gate, and the hut-to-hut experience you already have suggests you can handle the format. I could not confirm the booking window, the per-night fees, or which huts are open in your dates, and the access needs question was not answered, so ask the park directly about accessibility before relying on this.

candidatesAccepted.title: Navigation kit for cloud conditions
candidatesAccepted.summary: You said you would rather not learn to navigate in cloud on this trip, so a GPS unit with the park's topographic map loaded, plus a compass you have practised with, reduces that risk. I do not know whether the park rents these or what they cost, so check availability and terms with the park or a local outfitter.

candidatesAccepted.title: Satellite messenger for emergencies
candidatesAccepted.summary: The park has little or no mobile coverage in the backcountry, so a satellite messenger gives you a way to call for help if something goes wrong on a route with no road access. I have not checked rental availability or whether the park requires one, so confirm both before counting on it.
